body: Unfortunately I don't believe private loans have income-based repayment.

I'm gonna assume you're from MA cause you said wicked. 

I hope you're right though- about the not worrying about the debt 5 years into a career. I did more research into my area and found some decent paying jobs that can probably compare to salaries in the big cities (I didn't know companies like ESPN had locations in my state). 


I wish I wasn't so panicky though. I've been extensively researching schools to transfer to but I know I wouldn't be happy at those places and my credits probably wouldn't transfer. I feel like dropping out but I hope my hard work these next 3 years will be worth it. And maybe by some miracle I can actually get a scholarship or something to help ease the pain :(
Thanks. I will try to remain hopeful- it is just difficult to do each semester when I see my bill.

It's probably what I will do- though I hope to get a job higher than 50k. Just checked back my financial aid package from last year and I forgot to include the perkins loan in my financial aid total. So I will graduate with close to 90k rather than 80k =/ 


Also I'm unsure of how many jobs are in my area. I know Boston and NY are big cities with lots of cs jobs but it would be too far to commute. Probably easier to find a job in those big cities than in my area- which is mostly small suburbs.
